alex.k: Heads up — since ~05:20 UTC we're seeing a sustained capacity drop in eu-west-1. Latency up, queue length rising. Corrected ECC errors spiking across multiple racks :rotating_light:
priya_s: Details? numbers? which clusters?
alex.k: Corrected ECC errors/sec aggregated ~2400 across ~420 GPUs in cluster-eu-prod-1 and cluster-eu-prod-2. Observed increased KV cache misses too. Some pods hitting 504s.
chris_l: Ouch. Any recent driver/kernel/firmware pushes?
jordan_ops: No infra deploys in last 24h. Last change was a config push to autoscaler last week.
priya_s: I pulled a sample from rack-7 node-3: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows Correctable Errors: 186, Uncorrectable: 0, memory utilization normal. But errors are continuous.
alex.k: Also seeing repeated PCIe hot-reset attempts in dmesg on those nodes. Log snippet:
```
[ 1252.873456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID 0, GPU 0a, something
[ 1252.874001] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received
```
chris_l: Xid 31 but mostly corrected ECC. Could be noisy/freezing errors causing card slowdowns. Thermal? power?
jordan_ops: Checked datacenter BMS for rack-7: inlet temps normal, PSU rails steady. Vendor telemetry shows no immediate power alarms.
priya_s: I'm starting graceful drains on the most-affected nodes to reduce 504s. Command I'm running: `kubectl drain node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
sre-oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance ticket created: RDW-7843. Auto-scaler alerted and shifted some pods to other AZs, but capacity in eu-west is tight.
alex.k: Request: avoid new large batch jobs in eu-west until we triage. Please use eu-central or us-west if latency allows.
chris_l: Any sign it’s a firmware regression? Which GPU SKU?
jordan_ops: Affected nodes are A100-s 40GB NVLINK config, mostly machines deployed Q1 '24. Firmware versions are mixed; some nodes on v54, some on v56.
priya_s: I'm correlating error timestamps with firmware versions now. Early signal: nodes on v56 have 3x corrected errors relative to v54.
chris_l: If v56 is noisy we should consider rolling back driver/fw on a small canary set, but that’s heavy. Alternative: set scheduler nodeAffinity to avoid the worst hosts and rely on spare capacity.
alex.k: Short-term plan: 1) Continue draining top noisy nodes (priya). 2) Add node taints to prevent new pods (chris). 3) Kick off vendor RMA for persistent cards (jordan). 4) Update runbook and incident ticket (alex).
jordan_ops: I've opened a vendor escalation with telemetry dump attached. RMA pre-authorization requested for 6 cards.
priya_s: Drain progress: 18/32 marked cordoned and drained in cluster-eu-prod-1. Latency already improved on a handful of routes.
chris_l: Taint command I'm using: `kubectl taint nodes node-xyz gpu-health=degraded:NoSchedule` then add fallback routing in our service mesh to prefer other regions.
alex.k: Note — freight cost for cross-region fallbacks could spike. Finance flagged any >10% cross-region egress yesterday. Keep product informed.
jordan_ops: I've scheduled a rolling reboot window for the remaining nodes after drain completes — might clear transient PCIe issues.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident severity elevated to P2; paging on-call infra lead.
priya_s: Early correlation shows kernel AER handling rate skyrocketed; I'm grabbing kernel ring buffer for nodes going to vendor.
chris_l: For mid-term: add stronger telemetry for corrected ECC rates per-PCIe link, and surface anomaly alerts at lower thresholds. This would give us earlier warning.
alex.k: Agreed. Also flagging for infra roadmap: fleet firmware homogeneity and preflight firmware validation before rolling.
jordan_ops: I'll keep the RMA lane open. Next update in 20m after more drains complete.
priya_s: Update: after draining 28 nodes, corrected ECC/sec in cluster-eu-prod-1 fell from 2400 to ~320. Perf improved on p99 inference latency ~12% better.
alex.k: Great progress — thanks team. Leaving this thread open until vendor completes replacement and we confirm stable metrics for 24h. :thumbsup:
